source_refs.note: Exercise 6.1, Question 5: circle through two points with centre on x + y = 3; does (4, 1) lie on it; book p. 173, answers p. 304 (PDF 306)

blocks.prompt: 5. Find the equation of a circle passing through the points \((1, 3)\), \((2, -1)\) and having its centre on the line \(x + y = 3\). Does the point \((4, 1)\) lie on the circle?
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do points diye hain aur ek line jis par centre hai: yeh 6.1.5 ka Case-2 hai.
Diya kya hai? Points \((1, 3)\), \((2, -1)\) aur centre line \(x + y = 3\) par.
Find kya karna hai? Circle ki equation, aur yeh ke \((4, 1)\) circle par hai ya nahi.
Rule kaunsa? General form; do points se do equations, aur centre \((-g, -f)\) ko line mein rakhne se teesri.
Plan: \(g, f, c\) nikalo, equation likho, phir \((4, 1)\) rakh kar dekho ke zero aata hai ya nahi.
steps:
Diya gaya: circle \((1, 3)\) aur \((2, -1)\) se guzarta hai; centre \(x + y = 3\) par hai.
Maloom karna: equation; aur kya \((4, 1)\) circle par hai.
Tareeqa: General form mein teen unknowns. Do points se do equations, aur "centre line par hai" se teesri equation milti hai.

Circle farz karein aur \((1, 3)\) rakhein
\[x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\]
\[1 + 9 + 2g + 6f + c = 0\]
\[2g + 6f + c + 10 = 0 \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Circle par pada point equation ko satisfy karta hai.

Centre line par
\[(-g) + (-f) = 3\]
\[g + f = -3 \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Centre \((-g, -f)\) hai, aur jo point line par ho woh line ki equation ko satisfy karta hai.
Dhyan dein: Line mein \(g\) aur \(f\) nahi, \(-g\) aur \(-f\) rakhne hain; yahi sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(c\) khatam karein
\[(1) - (2):\ -2g + 8f + 5 = 0 \quad (4)\]
Kyun: Dono mein \(c\) hai, minus se ud gaya: \(2g - 4g = -2g\), \(6f + 2f = 8f\), \(10 - 5 = 5\).

(3) aur (4) hal karein
\[g = -3 - f\]
\[-2(-3 - f) + 8f + 5 = 0\]
\[10f + 11 = 0,\quad f = -\tfrac{11}{10}\]
\[g = -3 + \tfrac{11}{10} = -\tfrac{19}{10}\]
Kyun: (3) se \(g\) nikal kar (4) mein rakha: \(6 + 2f + 8f + 5 = 0\), yani \(10f = -11\). Phir \(f\) ki value (3) mein wapas rakh kar \(g\) nikala. Fractions se ghabrayein nahi; is sawal ka centre waqai \(\left(\frac{19}{10}, \frac{11}{10}\right)\) hai, jo poore numbers nahi.

(1) se \(c\) nikalein
\[-\tfrac{38}{10} - \tfrac{66}{10} + c + 10 = 0\]
\[c = \tfrac{104}{10} - 10 = \tfrac{2}{5}\]
Kyun: \(2g = -\frac{38}{10}\) aur \(6f = -\frac{66}{10}\); in ka jama \(-\frac{104}{10}\) hai. To \(c = \frac{104}{10} - \frac{100}{10} = \frac{4}{10} = \frac{2}{5}\). Kisi bhi point wali equation se \(c\) nikal sakte the, jawab wohi aata.

Equation
\[x^2 + y^2 - \tfrac{19}{5}x - \tfrac{11}{5}y + \tfrac{2}{5} = 0\]
\[5x^2 + 5y^2 - 19x - 11y + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: \(2g = -\frac{19}{5}\), \(2f = -\frac{11}{5}\). Fractions hatane ke liye poori equation ko 5 se multiply kiya; is se circle nahi badalta.

Kya \((4, 1)\) circle par hai?
\[5(16) + 5(1) - 19(4) - 11(1) + 2\]
\[= 80 + 5 - 76 - 11 + 2 = 0\]
Kyun: Left side bilkul zero aaya, matlab point equation ko satisfy karta hai, yani circle par hai. Agar zero se zyada aata to bahar, kam aata to andar (6.2.4 wala rule).

Tasdeeq
\[\text{centre} = \left(\tfrac{19}{10}, \tfrac{11}{10}\right)\]
\[\tfrac{19}{10} + \tfrac{11}{10} = 3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Centre line \(x + y = 3\) par hai. Aur \((2, -1)\) rakhein: \(20 + 5 - 38 + 11 + 2 = 0\) \(\checkmark\).
